heroHeadline: Puerto Rico Senate Hears Agencies Oppose Esencia Megaproject Bad Bunny Targeted Onstage
heroSubtitle: The fallout from Bad Bunny's Hiram Bithorn tour finale keeps rippling through Puerto Rico's government. On August 27, the Senate's Commission on Innovation, Reform and Appointments heard the Aqueduct and Sewer Authority, the Electric Power Authority, and the Puerto Rico Tourism Company all testify against the roughly $2 billion Proyecto Esencia megaproject in Cabo Rojo — the same project Bad Bunny demanded be "canceled" from the stage on August 22-23 and that thousands marched against in Cabo Rojo on August 23. PRASA's own engineer told Senate President Rivera Schatz the system "does not have the capacity" to serve the project, PREPA warned added well pumping could degrade the water resource, and advocates flagged a saltwater-intrusion risk near Peñones de Melones; Senator Eliezer Molina said it was the first time in his career he'd seen permits granted over unanimous agency opposition. A follow-up hearing with OGPe, natural-resources regulators, and the project's developers is expected the following Tuesday. The hearing came days after a federal judge separately denied Bad Bunny $465,612 in legal fees despite his dismissed copyright win over Nigerian producer Dera and emPawa Africa.
